docs.title: Main page
docs.text:
NEOTOKYO Rebuild is a tactical first-person shooter, rebuilt on the 2025 Source SDK. This wiki is its reference.

Every stat here comes from the game's source code, and links to the line it came from.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Getting started

    The rules every new player gets wrong: no headshot bonus, one life per round, ranks unlock guns.

  • Capture the Ghost

    The core mode. Find the ghost, carry it home, or wipe the other team.

  • Classes

    Recon, Assault and Support: health, speed, cloak and vision compared.

docs.title: Combat
docs.text:
• Weapons

    Damage, rate of fire, penetration and shots to kill, side by side.

    SRM · ZR68C · MX · SRS · PZ252 …

  • Damage & penetration

    The ×1.485 damage modifier, hit locations, how well bullets go through each material, and accuracy.

  • Loadouts & ranks

    How much XP each gun needs, and how to earn it.

    Dog · Pvt · Cpl · Sgt · Lt

docs.title: Player mechanics
docs.text:
• Thermoptic camo

    13 seconds for Recon, 8 seconds for Assault, and what gives a cloaked player away.

  • Vision modes

    Night, motion and thermal: which ones see through cloak and smoke.

  • Movement

    How fast you move with each weapon, plus leaning and fall damage.

  • AUX power

    How fast each class spends and regains AUX, and why Recon sprints for free.

    Where it spawns, its beacon, the rules for whoever carries it, and what happens when it's dropped.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: NT;RE plays differently from most shooters. These are the rules that decide fights. Each one links to the full detail.

docs.title: 1. You get one life per round
docs.text:
In Capture the Ghost, the main mode, you don't respawn until the next round. A round is about 3 minutes of play, after a 15-second freeze.

A round ends when:

  • someone captures the ghost
  • one team is wiped out
  • time runs out. That's a draw, whichever team holds the ghost.

docs.title: 2. Headshots aren't special
docs.text:
Aim at centre mass. A hit to the head does no more damage than a hit to the chest:

  • head and chest: ×1.0
  • stomach and arms: ×0.75
  • legs: ×0.6

There's no damage falloff over distance. Every bullet does ×1.485 its listed base damage. See Damage & penetration.

docs.title: 3. Your class decides how you fight
docs.text: Class Play it as Key trait Recon Scout, flanker Free sprint, 13 s cloak, super jump; only 100 HP Assault Rifleman Motion vision spots moving cloakers; widest gun choice Support Anchor, suppression 225 HP, thermal sees through smoke; can't sprint or cloak

docs.title: 4. XP unlocks weapons
docs.text:
XP raises your rank, and each rank unlocks better primaries.

  • A kill, an assist or a round win earns 1 XP.
  • A teamkill or a suicide costs 1 XP.
  • A ghost capture moves every surviving teammate straight up to the next rank.

A capture is worth far more than a few kills. XP resets at the start of every match. See Loadouts & ranks.

docs.title: 5. Watch what's in your hands
docs.text:
The weapon you're holding sets how fast you move. It ranges from ×1.0 down to ×0.675 for the PZ252.

To rotate faster, switch to your sidearm or knife (×0.85). See Movement.

docs.title: 6. The cloak isn't invisibility
docs.text:
Thermoptic camouflage, the cloak, is hard to see while you stand still. But Assault's motion vision highlights you the moment you move.

Switching the cloak on makes you flash, and so does firing an unsuppressed weapon. Suppressed weapons keep you hidden.

docs.title: 7. Don't shoot teammates early
docs.text: Friendly fire is on. For the first 7 seconds of each round, damage you do to teammates is reflected back to you at double strength. See Team damage.

docs.title: About this wiki
docs.text:
This is a prototype wiki for NEOTOKYO Rebuild (NT;RE). It's built with MkDocs and the Material theme.

Its job is to settle the structure, page types and visual design. An earlier static HTML prototype sits alongside it in prototype/, for comparison.

docs.title: How the numbers are sourced
docs.text:
Every stat on this site was extracted from the NeotokyoRebuild/neo repository. It comes from one of two places: the weapon scripts in game/neo/scripts/, or the C++ gameplay code in src/game/.

Each number has a footnote that links to the exact file and line it came from. The links are pinned to a specific commit (see the page footer).

Tables and stat blocks are generated from the data when the site is built, so no number is typed by hand twice. When the game changes, the data can be re-extracted and every page rebuilt.

docs.title: Page types demonstrated
docs.text:
• Hub pages: Main page, Weapons, Classes, Game modes
  • Weapon pages: one Markdown file per weapon, in a fixed layout (overview, general stats, damage, shots to kill, time to kill, handling, availability). You can edit the prose by hand. Every number comes from a {{weapon:…}} snippet.
  • Mechanic articles: hand-written explanations with citations, such as Thermoptic camouflage and Damage & penetration
  • Reference tables: Console variables, Maps, Loadouts & ranks

docs.title: Not in the prototype
docs.text:
• Editing and page history. Pages are Markdown files in the repository.
  • Images. Grey boxes mark where screenshots or renders would go, until asset licensing is decided.
  • Lore and story. This pass covers gameplay mechanics and stats only.
  • Terminology and external resources pages.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
In wiki/, install the requirements with pip install -r requirements.txt, then run mkdocs serve.

  • Pages live in docs/.
  • Extracted game data lives in data/.
  • Snippets, wiki links and citations are handled by hooks/ntre.py and hooks/generators.py.

See Style guide for the markup.

docs.text:
The wiki's palette follows the NEOTOKYO;REBUILD branding: neutral black, white and a red dot. One cool accent is added for link underlines.

Red is kept to small marks. It never colours link text, because on a wiki red text means a page that doesn't exist yet.

docs.title: Style guide
docs.text: The rules every page on this wiki follows. The writing rules live in WRITING-STYLE.md at the top of the repository and are included here, so this page always matches them.

docs.title: Who we write for
docs.text:
Players. Someone between rounds who wants an answer, or someone new who wants to understand a mechanic. They know shooters and the game's own terms (HP, XP, AUX, sprint, loadout). They don't know Source engine internals or C++, and they shouldn't need to.

Their attention is limited, so every sentence has to earn its place.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
• Plain and direct. Address the player as you, in the present tense.
  • Open with what the thing is and why it matters. Name the subject in bold in the first sentence.
  • Lead with what it means for the player: what to do, what to expect, what to avoid. How the code does it comes second, if at all.
  • One idea per sentence. Keep sentences short, and paragraphs to one to three sentences.
  • Use everyday words. Say hitbox, not hull. Leave out function names, file names and engine terms like tick and renormalised unless the reader needs them; if they do, explain the term once.
  • Cut filler, hype and hedging that carries no information.
  • British spelling (colour, armour, behaviour). Code identifiers and quoted strings keep their own spelling.
  • Headings in sentence case: Weapon speed scale, not Weapon Speed Scale.

docs.title: Keep the load light
docs.text:
• No more than two numbers in a sentence. Round in prose ("about 24 seconds") and give exact figures in tables and infoboxes.
  • Move the mechanics out of the way. Formulas, code behaviour and edge cases most readers can skip go in a collapsed Technical details box at the end of the section. The box keeps its citations, so nothing is lost.
  • Put server settings last. Console variables only server admins can change go under a For server admins heading at the end of the page.
  • Use lists for sets of conditions, and tables for comparisons. A sentence that lists four conditions is a list.
  • One caveat, once. If something is unconfirmed, say so in one callout, not in every sentence that touches it.

For example, instead of:

Each cloaked player has a visibility factor from 0 to 1 that controls how strong the shimmer and tint are. Standing still (≤20 u/s) lowers it by 1.1 per second; moving raises it by speed × 0.004 per second.

write:

The faster you move, the more you shimmer. Stand still and the shimmer fades in about a second.

and put the first version in the Technical details box.

docs.title: Facts and sources
docs.text:
• Every gameplay number cites the line it comes from. [[src:path:line]] becomes a footnote linked to the game's source at the pinned commit.
  • Never guess. If the code is ambiguous, or client and server disagree, say so in an amber callout labelled Unconfirmed, Unverified or Unresolved.
  • Say how a claim was established: "inferred from the code" is different from "tested in game".
  • Tables and infoboxes take their numbers from the extracted data, not from hand-typed copies.
  • Rewording must not change a fact. Rounding in prose is fine when the exact figure is in a table, infobox or Technical details box on the same page.

docs.title: Numbers and units
docs.text:
Spell units out in prose and abbreviate them in data. Prose is anything written as a sentence: paragraphs, list items, callouts and table captions. Data is table cells, infobox values and stat strips.

Quantity In prose In data Time 2.16 seconds, 250 milliseconds, 3.25 minutes 2.16 s, 250 ms, 3.25 min Speed 256 units per second 256 u/s Distance 150 units; metres only where the game uses them 150 u, 45.72 m Angle 1 degree 1° Multiplier ×0.85, times sign and no space ×0.85 Range 0.675–1.0, en dash and no spaces 0.675–1.0 Damage Effective damage, with the ×1.485 modifier applied, unless labelled base 17.82 (base 12) Game terms HP, XP, AUX, RPM: players know these, so keep them short 225 HP

As an adjective, hyphenate: a 10-second delay, a 13-second cloak.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
• Weapons use their in-game display names: MPN45, SRM-S, ZR68-L, Murata Supa-7, MilSO.
  • Classes are capitalised: Recon, Assault, Support.
  • In tight table columns, Recon, Assault and Support shorten to R, A and S, always in that order. Where a column also gives the XP a class needs, write the letter and the number together: R4 A10 S20. A letter alone means no XP is needed. The column's tooltip explains the notation, and each entry has its own tooltip naming the class and the rank.
  • Game modes take the full name first, then the code: Capture the Ghost (CTG).
  • Teams: Jinrai and NSF. The objective is the ghost, lowercase in running text.
  • Thermoptic camouflage is the cloak after its first mention.
  • Console variables and file names go in code, with their default where it matters: mp_friendlyfire 1.

docs.title: Page anatomy
docs.text:
1. A # Title, and a one-line description in the front matter
  2. A lead of one or two short paragraphs that stands on its own
  3. An infobox for classes, modes and mechanics with stats
  4. Sections under ## headings. The contents list on the right is automatic.
  5. For server admins, if the page has any
  6. The generated references, last

Weapon pages follow one layout, in this order: Overview, General stats, Damage, Shots to kill, Time to kill, Handling, then anything weapon-specific (bolt action, heat), Availability, Suppressor and Technical notes. The prose is yours to write; the numbers come from {{weapon:…}} snippets, which read the weapon named in the front matter (weapon: weapon_zr68s).

  • Comparisons go in tables, not lists. Numbers are right-aligned in monospace.
  • Every column header in a data table has a tooltip saying what it means. Shared headers are defined once in COLUMN_TIPS in wiki/hooks/generators.py; a table where a header means something different passes its own. The build warns about any header without one.
  • Hit locations with the same multiplier share a column: head / chest, stomach / arms, legs.
  • Link a page's first mention in each section, not every mention.
  • Page addresses follow the menu: /weapons/rifles/zr68-s/. Folders and file names are lowercase with hyphens, and every slug is unique across the wiki.

docs.title: Markup
docs.text:
• [[slug|Label]] links to another page. A slug is the file name without .md, or the folder name for an index.md.
  • [[slug#heading|Label]] links to a section of another page.
  • [[src:path:line]] is a citation. Separate several with ;.
  • {{table:…}}, {{stat:…}} and {{weapon:…}} insert tables and numbers generated from the data.
  • !!! info "Label" is a neutral callout, for notes.
  • !!! warning "Label" is an amber callout, for anything quirky, unverified or in progress.
  • ??? note "Technical details" is the collapsed box for mechanics most readers can skip.

Indent a callout's or box's body by four spaces.

docs.title: Rewriting a page
docs.text:
When you reword an existing page, for clarity or to bring it up to this guide:

  • Keep every citation, word for word. Move it with the fact it supports, for example into a Technical details box, but never drop or edit it.
  • Don't lose a number. If one leaves the main text, it goes into the Technical details box. Rounding in prose is fine when the exact figure stays on the page.
  • Don't change a fact or add one. If you can't say something more simply without changing what it means, leave it as it is.
  • Leave generated parts alone: {{…}} snippets, infobox data and table cells. Table captions are prose, so reword those.
  • Check links before renaming a heading. Other pages link to sections with [[page#heading|…]]; search for the heading's anchor first.
  • Build with mkdocs build --strict (from wiki/). It fails on broken links and unknown snippets.

docs.title: Modes in development
docs.text:
• Game modes still in development are named only on their own pages, along with the roles they assign and the weapons those roles use. Nothing else in the wiki mentions them: not class, weapon, mode or map lists, not comparisons, not the main page, not this guide.
  • Their own pages open with an amber Work in progress callout and a neutral Not a class you can pick callout, and hold everything about the mode: its role, the role's stats and weapon, and its server settings.
  • Text that comes from the data is filtered so it doesn't name them. The build warns about any page that does.

docs.title: Visual
docs.text:
• Dark by default, minimal, neutral, with a light theme one click away. Hairline borders; no shadows, gradients or emoji.
  • Blocks are rounded: 8px on tables, callouts, cards, infoboxes, code and the search box; 6px on navigation items.

  • Text uses four sizes, set as tokens in ntre.css (in rem, so they follow Material's scaling and the reader's browser settings). At the default size:

    • Prose, 14px: body text, lists, card titles
    • Secondary, 12px: callouts and Technical details, card text, the menu and contents, search, references, footer, infobox titles
    • Data, 10.8px: tables and their captions, stat strips, infobox rows, tags, keys
    • Marks, 9px at least: citation markers, so they stay clickable in tables

    Headings scale from the prose size. - Red is for the brand dot only: after page titles and beside the current page. Never for link text, because red text means a missing page. - Link underlines are a cool, desaturated cyan. On hover the line fills left to right, snaps into place, pulses once and settles. Cards lift to a lighter surface on hover instead. - The NT;RE mark is the primary logo. The wordmark appears only on the main page. - Image slots are grey placeholders labelled with what belongs there, until assets are licensed.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
Every player in NT;RE picks one of three classes: Recon, Assault or Support. Your class sets your health, speed and vision mode, whether you can cloak, and which primary weapons you can choose at each rank.

The two teams, Jinrai and NSF, play the same. They differ only in player models, HUD colour and which spawn they start from.

docs.title: Choosing and changing class
docs.text:
A class change takes effect straight away when:20

  • you're dead
  • it's the freeze before the round, and you haven't fired or dropped a weapon
  • it's warmup
  • you're playing Deathmatch or Team Deathmatch and spawned less than 10 seconds ago

Otherwise the change waits until your next spawn.

Servers can limit or ban classes. If the class you ask for is full, you get the first class that isn't.2122

docs.title: Shared rules
docs.text:
• No armour. Health is all you have. No class takes reduced damage.23
  • Your weapon sets your speed. Every weapon scales your class speed by ×0.675–1.0. See Movement.
  • A knife backstab kills any class. It does exactly 226 damage, one more than Support's maximum health.24
  • No prone. You can stand, crouch and lean, and that's all.

docs.title: For server admins
docs.text: sv_neo_class_limit_recon, sv_neo_class_limit_assault and sv_neo_class_limit_support cap each class. The default, -1, means no limit, and 0 bans the class.2122

Assault is the all-rounder. It has more health than Recon, a short cloak, and motion vision that picks out anything that moves.

It also has the widest choice of primary weapons in the game, from SMGs up to the SRS sniper rifle and AA13 auto-shotgun.

docs.title: Strengths and weaknesses
docs.text:
• Biggest sprint boost. Sprinting takes you from 160 to 256 units per second. Recon still sprints faster, at 270.14
  • Sprinting costs AUX. A full bar lasts 20 seconds of sprinting, and it doesn't refill while you sprint.15
  • Slows on landing. After a jump you're slowed for 1.15 seconds, like every class except Recon.
Technical details
  • Assault sprints at ×1.6 its run speed. Recon sprints at ×1.35.14
  • Sprinting drains 5 AUX per second while you're moving. Each time you stop sprinting, another 0.5 AUX is taken.15

docs.title: Motion vision
docs.text:
Motion vision highlights anything that moves, and that includes cloaked players. A cloaked enemy who stands perfectly still disappears again.16

See Vision modes.

Technical details

Any model moving faster than 0.5 units per second is drawn with an extra highlight pass.16

docs.title: Thermoptic camouflage
docs.text:
Assault's cloak lasts 8 seconds, and takes 32 seconds to refill from empty.17

See Thermoptic camouflage for what gives a cloaked player away.

Technical details

The cloak recharges at 0.25 per second.17

Recon is the scout. It's the fastest class, with the longest cloak and a super jump.

The trade-off is health: Recon has the least of the three main classes, and the fewest primary weapons to choose from.

docs.title: Strengths and weaknesses
docs.text:
• Fastest. Runs at 2002 units per second and sprints at 27034. Assault manages 160 and 256.
  • Sprints for free. Sprinting costs no AUX, and AUX keeps recharging while you run.15 You only spend AUX on the super jump.
  • Lands cleanly. Other classes slow down for a moment after landing a jump. Recon doesn't.16
  • Jumps highest. 54 units, half again the normal height.17
  • Fragile. 100 HP, the lowest of any class.

docs.title: Super jump
docs.text:
Hold Sprint, then press Jump while moving forward or backward. You leap forward as well as up. It costs 45 AUX.1819

It only works when:20

  • you're sprinting on the ground, and not wading
  • you're not carrying the ghost
  • you have at least 45 AUX

Look straight ahead when you jump. Looking up or down makes the leap shorter.21

Unconfirmed: strafing wastes the jump

Holding only a strafe key seems to spend the 45 AUX without the forward leap. Strafing while holding forward seems to shorten it. This comes from reading the code and hasn't been tested in play.22

Technical details
  • The leap adds your current maximum speed on top of a normal jump.18
  • It follows your view direction with the vertical part removed but not renormalised, so it shrinks by the cosine of your pitch.21
  • The 45 AUX is taken whenever the conditions above pass, but the boost only applies if exactly one of forward or back is held. With a strafe key held alongside, it's scaled by ×0.707.22

Support is the heavy class. With 225 HP it can take almost twice the punishment of an Assault. It can't sprint and can't cloak.

Thermal vision shows uncloaked players as hot silhouettes, even through smoke. Support is also the only class that can carry the PZ252 machine gun.

docs.title: Strengths and weaknesses
docs.text:
• Most health. 225, the most of any class you can pick, with no armour on top.11 Only a knife backstab (226 damage) is guaranteed to kill you outright.12
  • Sees through smoke. Smoke isn't drawn while thermal vision is on.13
  • Can't sprint.1415
  • No AUX and no cloak. Support doesn't use AUX at all, and has no thermoptic camouflage.
  • Biggest target. Standing, Support is 70 units tall, the largest of the classes you can pick.
Technical details

The code has a Support sprint speed of 216, but it's commented as reserved for future use.1415

docs.title: Thermal vision and cloak
docs.text: Thermal vision shows uncloaked players, NPCs and corpses as hot. Cloaked players don't glow. They look normal, with no heat highlight, so they don't stand out against the cold background the way you might expect.16

docs.text:
Capture the Ghost (CTG) is NT;RE's core competitive mode, and 24 of the official maps are built for it.

Alongside it are two respawn modes, Team Deathmatch (TDM) and Deathmatch (DM).

docs.title: Round flow
docs.text:
All the scored modes follow the same cycle:12

  1. Warmup (45 seconds). This runs once, when a match starts. You respawn freely and XP doesn't count.13
  2. Pre-round freeze (15 seconds). You can look around and change loadout, but you can't move. You can't be hurt either.14
  3. Live round. The freeze counts towards the round timer, so a 3.25-minute CTG round has about 3 minutes of live play.15
  4. Overtime, where the mode has it.
  5. Post-round (15 seconds), then the next freeze.16

When warmup ends, team scores and rounds won reset to 0. So does every player's XP.17 The teams swap spawn sides and capture zones every round.18

A round won't start while either team is empty. The game tries again every 10 seconds.19

In one-life modes, you can still spawn for up to 15 seconds after the freeze ends.20

docs.title: Match length
docs.text:
• The score limit counts rounds won, not kills.21
  • If there's a round limit, the match ends early once the trailing team can no longer catch up.22
  • If rounds won are tied when the limit is reached, play goes to sudden death. It continues until a team wins a round.23

docs.title: Choosing the mode
docs.text:
Each map sets its own mode by default. A map that doesn't falls back to Free Roam.24 Servers can override this: see For server admins.

Technical details

A map sets its mode through a neo_game_config entity.24

docs.title: Competitive features
docs.text:
CTG supports competitive extras:25

  • a ready-up lobby, 5 players per team by default
  • .pause and .unpause, for 60 seconds or 180 seconds
  • spectators can only watch their own team
  • paired ghost spawns

docs.title: Other modes
docs.text:
• Training (TUT): tutorial maps (ntre_class_tut, ntre_shooting_tut) with no round logic. Completing them earns achievements.26
  • Free Roam (EMT): no objective and no scoring. You can change team, class and loadout while alive.11

docs.title: Bots
docs.text:
Bots know how to play CTG: they seek, carry and escort the ghost, and some lie in wait as lone wolves. In TDM and DM they just hunt down enemies.

You can command bots with Use.2728

  • sv_neo_latespawn_max_time sets the 15-second late-spawn window in one-life modes.20
  • Sudden death needs neo_round_sudden_death 1.23
  • sv_neo_comp 1 turns on all the competitive features at once.25

docs.text:
Capture the Ghost Ghost capture screenshot CodeCTG Mapsntre_*_ctg (24) Round3.251 min Match to72 rounds LivesOne per round Capture timeInstant

Capture the Ghost (CTG) is NT;RE's core mode. Each round, an AI core called the ghost spawns somewhere on the map.

A team wins the round by carrying the ghost into its capture zone, or by wiping out the enemy team. You get one life per round.

docs.title: Winning a round
docs.text:
• Ghost capture: a live player carrying the ghost enters the radius of an active capture zone owned by their team (or a neutral zone) while the round is live. The round is won instantly; there is no hold timer.34
  • Team elimination: the enemy team has 0 living members. If both teams reach 0 at once, the round is a stalemate.5
  • Time runs out with no capture or elimination: stalemate ('TIE'). Neither team gets a round win and nobody gets round-end XP.6
Technical details

As extracted from the code:

  • Map logic can force a winner through neo_game_config FireTeamWin / FireRoundTie inputs.7

Time-out is always a draw

When the clock runs out, it's a stalemate. It doesn't matter who holds the ghost or how many players are alive. The code has a "win by numbers" outcome, but nothing triggers it.8

docs.title: Capture zones
docs.text:
A capture zone belongs to one team or is neutral. The zones swap between the teams every round, along with the spawns.15

The capture counts the instant a living ghost carrier reaches the zone. There's no hold timer.16

Technical details

Capture zones are neo_ghost_retrieval_point entities. The game checks them 10 times a second, using the 3D distance from the zone's centre to see whether the carrier is within the zone's radius.16

docs.title: Overtime
docs.text:
Overtime is off by default. When it's on, the round can run past the clock while someone is carrying the ghost. Dropping the ghost cuts the extra time short.17

Technical details

Overtime starts when the ghost is being carried with 10 seconds or less left. The round can then run up to 45 seconds past the limit while the ghost stays in hand. If the carrier drops it, the time left shrinks back to the 10-second grace.17

docs.title: XP and rewards
docs.text:
A ghost capture is the most valuable thing you can do in NT;RE. Every surviving player on the capturing team goes straight up to the next rank. Dead teammates get the normal +1.18

Winning by elimination gives:19

  • +1 to the whole team
  • +1 more to each survivor
  • +1 more to the ghost carrier, so a surviving carrier gets +3

See Loadouts & ranks.

Technical details

Surviving capturers are raised straight to the next rank threshold: 0 → 4 → 10 → 20.18

docs.title: Cap prevention
docs.text:
Sometimes the enemy is carrying the ghost when the last living player on your team:

  • kills themselves
  • disconnects
  • dies to their own team's grenade

The enemy team then still gets the capture reward when it wins the round.20

  • When a winner is decided the game goes to intermission (map end).3

The ghost is the objective in Capture the Ghost (CTG). Whoever carries it can see every enemy within about 46 metres.

The catch: everyone else on the map can see where the carrier is.

docs.title: Picking it up
docs.text:
• It goes in the primary slot. You can't pick it up while holding a primary weapon, so drop yours first.4
  • It can't shoot or aim.5
  • Picking it up stops your sprint. You can't use the Recon super jump while you carry it.67

Unconfirmed

Whether a carrier can sprint again after picking it up is unclear. The client blocks it, but the server's check doesn't mention the ghost. This needs testing in game.

docs.title: Enemy beacons
docs.text:
Hold the ghost as your active weapon. After a few seconds of boot-up, it marks every living enemy within about 46 metres with a red beacon, through walls. Each beacon shows how far away that enemy is.8

Your teammates don't see the beacons. Spectators watching you do.9

The ghost also beeps faster the closer the nearest enemy gets.10

Technical details
  • Boot-up takes 3.3 seconds. The beacons reach 45.72 metres (1800 units).8
  • The ghost beeps every 0.1 × distance in metres seconds, between 1 and 3.5 seconds.10

docs.title: Being the carrier
docs.text:
Everyone else sees a pulsing marker on the ghost or its carrier. It's red to the enemy and your team colour to friendlies.11

You can't bunny-hop the ghost across the map.12

Technical details

The carrier gets the objective air friction, which stops bunny-hopping.12

docs.title: Spawning and dropping
docs.text:
• One ghost spawns each round, at a random ghost spawn point.13 In competitive play, rounds come in pairs from the same spawn, so each team gets the same start once.14
  • It drops when the carrier dies or disconnects, or presses drop while holding it. A dropped ghost is never removed.1516
  • If it's thrown or carried out of bounds, it goes back to the last spot where its last carrier stood on solid ground.17

docs.title: For server admins
docs.text: sv_neo_ghost_spawn_bias pairs the ghost spawns as described above. It's on in competitive play.14

Work in progress

Juggernaut is still in development. Its rules and numbers are likely to change.

Not a class you can pick

The Juggernaut is a role the Juggernaut mode assigns. You can't choose it from the class menu, and it only exists in this mode.

In Juggernaut (JGR), both teams fight over a single JGR56 suit. Whoever activates it becomes the Juggernaut, with 990 HP, a BALC heat weapon and night vision.

While a team has the suit, its kills score points. The first team to 20 points wins the round.

docs.title: Winning a round
docs.text:
• A team reaches 20 team points while the round is live.12
  • Time-out with no living juggernaut, and nobody on the trailing team is mid-activation: the higher team score wins.13
  • Time-out with equal scores and no juggernaut: stalemate.14
  • Time-out while a juggernaut is alive, or while the trailing team is activating the suit: Overtime. Overtime ends when the juggernaut's team is ahead (they win), or when the juggernaut is gone and the first condition applies.15
Technical details

As extracted from the code:

  • A team reaches sv_neo_jgr_max_points (20) team points while the round is live.12

docs.title: The suit
docs.text:
• It spawns at a juggernaut spawn point each round. It stays locked until 20 seconds after the freeze ends ("JUGGERNAUT ENABLED").16
  • To activate it, stand within 150 units and hold Use for 5 seconds. You're frozen while you hold. Letting go, dying or moving away cancels it.17
  • When you activate it, you drop all your weapons and get full health and 100 AUX. Dead teammates respawn immediately.18
  • When the Juggernaut dies, the suit drops where they fell and can be taken again.19

docs.title: Playing as the Juggernaut
docs.text:
• 990 HP. You don't bleed and can't be gibbed.20
  • Your only weapon is the BALC. It has no magazine. It overheats after 50 shots and locks for 5 seconds, and has a charged grenade alt-fire. It doesn't slow you down (×1.0).
  • You can't pick up the ghost or any other weapon.
  • Everyone can always see your position on the compass.21
  • You jump 1.4 times as high as normal, to 50.4 units.22
  • Like the ghost carrier, you lose any speed above your run speed while airborne.23
  • One player model, shared by both teams.24
  • AUX regenerates at 10 per second.

Unresolved: sprint speed

The Juggernaut probably sprints at 256 units per second, but the code disagrees with itself. The movement code gives 256. The defined constant and GetSprintSpeed() say 270. This hasn't been checked in game yet.

docs.title: Team Deathmatch
docs.text:
Team Deathmatch (TDM) is a respawn mode. Two teams fight for one long round, and the team with the higher score when time runs out wins.

The official map is ntre_bullet_tdm.

docs.title: Winning
docs.text:
• When time runs out, the team with the higher team score wins the round.1
  • Equal team scores at time-out: stalemate.2
  • Match ends when a team reaches the score limit in rounds won (default 1, so the first round won ends the match).3

One round

The default score limit is 1 round won, so a TDM match is a single 10.25-minute round.4

Work in progress

VIP is still in development. Its rules and numbers are likely to change, and no official map is built for it yet.

Not a class you can pick

The VIP is a role the VIP mode assigns. You can't choose it from the class menu, and it only exists in this mode.

In Extract or Kill the VIP (VIP), one team escorts a lightly armed VIP to its extraction zone. The other team tries to kill them.

VIP is also the name of the special class the escorted player becomes. The mode uses the same capture zones as Capture the Ghost (CTG).

docs.title: Winning a round
docs.text:
• VIP escort: the VIP enters the radius of an active capture zone owned by their team (or a neutral zone) while the round is live.1213
  • VIP killed: the team opposing the escorting team wins.14
  • VIP disconnects: the opposing team wins by forfeit.15
  • Team elimination, same as CTG.16
  • Time runs out: stalemate.17
Technical details

As extracted from the code:

  • VIP escort: the VIP (class NEO_CLASS_VIP) enters the radius of an active capture zone owned by their team (or a neutral zone) while the round is live.1213
  • VIP killed: the team opposing the escorting team wins (when sv_neo_vip_ctg_on_death=0).14
  • VIP disconnects (m_pVIP becomes null): the opposing team wins by forfeit (when sv_neo_vip_ctg_on_death=0).15

The escorting team is picked at random in the first round, then the teams take turns.

The VIP is a random player on that team with cl_neo_vip_eligible 1, which is the default. If nobody has it set, anyone on the team can be picked.18

At the start of the next round, the VIP goes back to their previous class.19

docs.title: Damage & penetration
docs.text:
Damage in NT;RE is simple. A bullet does its weapon's damage, scaled by where it hits, and only loses damage when it passes through a wall.

There's no armour, no headshot bonus and no falloff over distance.

docs.title: How damage works
docs.text:
Every bullet's damage is scaled by ×1.485, then by the hit location.12

  • Range doesn't matter. A bullet does the same damage at any distance until it hits something.3
  • There's no armour. Classes differ only in how much health they have.4
  • Fractions add up. Each hit takes whole HP only. The leftover fraction is saved for each attacker, and taken once it reaches 1.5
Technical details
  • damage = weapon damage × 1.485 × hit-location multiplier [× penetration loss]12
  • The 1.485 is sv_neo_wep_dmg_modifier, applied to every bullet. Explosives use sv_neo_exp_dmg_modifier, also 1.485.6
  • Maximum health is 100 for Recon, 120 for Assault and 225 for Support.4

No headshot bonus

A headshot does exactly as much damage as a chest shot. NT;RE sets the head multiplier to 1.0, where Half-Life 2 uses 2.0.

docs.title: Penetration
docs.text:
Bullets can go through walls. Every gun has a penetration value, and every surface has a value for how easy it is to shoot through. Thinner walls, and surfaces like glass, are easier to get through.12

  • A bullet that goes through keeps at least a quarter of its damage.13
  • It can carry on through more walls with the penetration it has left.14
  • Bullets never pass through players.15
  • Shotgun pellets (buckshot) never go through anything. The Supa-7 slug does.

In the table, a higher value means the surface is easier to shoot through. Dirt and sand (0.2) are the hardest; glass (0.9) is easy.

Higher values are easier to shoot through. The third column is how much penetration a bullet needs to cross 12 units of that surface.SurfaceValuePen. to cross 12 uNotesdirt0.21660sand0.21760concrete0.31840metal0.51924computer0.52024tile0.52124flesh0.62220alienflesh0.62320grate0.752416vent0.752516wood0.752616plastic0.82715foliage0.82815glass0.92913.3antlion13012Index 0 is skipped by the 'material > 0' checkbloodyflesh13112eggshell13212clip13312blockbullets13412Never penetrable regardless of table valueslosh13512warpshield13612 Technical details
  • When a bullet hits a surface, the game measures how thick it is, up to 12 units, and divides that by the surface's value. If the result is no more than the bullet's remaining penetration, the bullet goes through.12
  • Damage after the wall is damage × max(0.25, 1 − used ÷ penetration), so a bullet keeps at least 25% of its damage.13
  • The penetration used is subtracted, and the bullet carries on with what's left.14
  • Buckshot has penetration 0.
  • The code calls the surface table PENETRATION_RESISTANCE, but its values work as a divisor, so a higher number means less resistance.

docs.title: Accuracy
docs.text:
Your shots spread wider when you fire, jump, or move without aiming, and tighten again when you stop. One shot pushes the spread most of the way to its maximum, so tap-firing and crouching matter.

Effect Penalty Each shot fired +0.837 Airborne, per second +3.038 Moving without aiming (speed > 5), per second +2.039 Recovery, per second −1.240 Extra recovery while crouched, per second −1.041

Changes to the accuracy penalty. The penalty runs from 0 to 1 and is capped at 1.0.

Unconfirmed: extra recoil on long bursts

The SRS and ZR68-L also add up to 1 degree of extra vertical recoil after 10 shots in a row. This comes from reading the code and hasn't been tested in play.42

Technical details

Each weapon has a minimum and maximum spread cone, one pair for hip fire and one for aiming. The current cone sits between them according to the accuracy penalty, from 0 to 1.43

docs.title: Team damage
docs.text:
Friendly fire is on by default, so you can hurt your teammates.51

For the first 7 seconds of a live round, it backfires. Your teammate takes no damage, and you take double what you dealt. If that kills you, you can't respawn that round.5253

docs.text:

  • sv_neo_hitboxgroup_pen 1 (default 0) changes how limb hits count. A shot that hits an arm or leg is traced again to see whether it would also have hit the head, chest or stomach behind it, and uses that multiplier instead.54

docs.title: Movement
docs.text:
How fast you move depends on your class, the weapon in your hands, your stance, and whether you're sprinting or aiming.

Speeds are in Hammer units per second. The base is 2001 units per second, which is Recon's run speed.

docs.title: What sets your speed
docs.text:
Your class sets your starting speed, and these change it:2

  • Weapon in hand. Each weapon slows you by its own amount. See below.
  • Crouching or walking each slow you by a quarter. Do both and you move at a little over half speed.
  • Sprinting speeds you up: by 35% for Recon and 60% for Assault. Support can't sprint.
  • Aiming down sights cuts your speed to 60%.
  • Moving backwards on the ground slows you by a further quarter.3
  • After a jump, every class except Recon is slowed for just over a second, most of all on landing.

However slow you get, you never drop below 55 units per second.

Technical details

Each tick, the game recomputes your maximum speed in this order:2

  1. Start from the class run speed: Recon 200, everyone else 160.
  2. Multiply by the active weapon's speed scale (0.675–1.0, see the table below).
  3. Crouching: ×0.75. Walking: ×0.75. The two stack, so a crouch-walk is ×0.5625.
  4. Sprinting: ×1.35 for Recon, ×1.6 for Assault. Support can't sprint.
  5. Aiming down sights: ×0.6.
  6. Never below 55 units per second.
  7. For 1.15 seconds after a jump, every class except Recon is slowed further. The penalty is strongest on landing and fades over that time, with a floor of 75 units per second.

Moving backwards on the ground is scaled by a further ×0.75.3

docs.title: Sprinting
docs.text:
• Sprinting uses 5 AUX per second, and only while you're actually moving. Recon sprints for free.52
  • You need at least 2 AUX to start.53
  • You can't aim while sprinting, and you can't sprint while carrying the ghost.5455

docs.title: Jumping
docs.text:
A normal jump is 36 units high. Recon jumps 54 units.56 Recon's super jump also leaps forward.

Crouch-jumping works as it does in standard Source games. NT;RE adds no bonus of its own.57

Technical details

Recon jumps 1.5× the default height (54 units).56

docs.title: Air control
docs.text: By default you lose no speed in the air. The ghost carrier is the exception: they lose any speed above their normal run speed while airborne. That stops them bunny-hopping the objective across the map.58

docs.title: Leaning
docs.text:
You can lean while you're alive, on the ground and not sprinting. Pressing both lean keys cancels the lean.59

Leans are asymmetric, to match the original NEOTOKYO: 7.5 units to the left and 15 to the right. A full lean takes 0.2 seconds.60 If there's no room, the lean is shortened.

Technical details

A full lean also rolls the camera 20 degrees and lowers your eyes by 2 units.60

docs.title: Footsteps
docs.text:
Footsteps start at 50 units per second.

While walking or aiming, you make no footstep sounds as long as you stay at or below 70% of your class's run speed. When crouched, it's 70% of your crouch speed.61

docs.title: Fall damage
docs.text:
Falls hurt once you land faster than 580 units per second. Even a fall at Source's nominal "fatal" speed of 1024 units per second does only about 25 damage.6263

Damage keeps rising steadily with speed above that, with no cap.

Technical details

Damage is (speed − 580) × 100 / 444 × 0.25, about 0.056 HP for every unit per second over the limit. It's linear and uncapped.6263

docs.title: For server admins
docs.text:
• sv_neo_airfriction sets how much speed above run speed is lost in the air. The default, 0, loses nothing.58
  • The ghost carrier uses sv_neo_airfriction_objective 0.5 instead.58
  • sv_neo_falldmg_scale is the 0.25 in the fall damage formula. It's why a fall at 1024 units per second does only about 25 damage.6263

Thermoptic camouflage, the cloak, makes you nearly invisible. Only Recon and Assault have it.6

The cloak has its own battery, so it never competes with sprinting or jumping for AUX.

docs.title: Battery
docs.text:
A full battery lasts 13 seconds for Recon and 8 seconds for Assault. It only recharges while the cloak is off.

Class Capacity Max duration Recharge /s Empty → full Recon 13 13 s 0.55 23.6 s Assault 8 8 s 0.25 32 s

Values from 7.

Technical details

The battery drains 1 unit per second, taken in whole-second steps. The cloak switches off when the battery drops to 0.1.2

docs.title: What gives you away
docs.text:
The cloak works best when you stand still. These give you away, worst first:

  • Motion vision. Assault players see anything that moves highlighted, cloaked or not.8
  • Moving. The faster you move, the more you shimmer. Stand still and the shimmer fades in about a second.9
  • Switching it on. You flash blue for half a second, and players nearby hear it.10
  • Firing. An unsuppressed weapon makes you flash. Suppressed weapons don't.11

Bots also find you more easily for a moment after you cloak or fire an unsuppressed weapon.12

In your favour: you cast no shadow while cloaked.13

docs.title: Against thermal vision
docs.text:
Support players see everyone glowing with heat, except cloaked players. You look normal to them, with no glow.14

Technical details
  • Motion vision highlights any model moving faster than 0.5 units per second.8
  • Each cloaked player has a visibility value from 0 to 1 that sets how strong the shimmer and tint are. Moving at 20 units per second or less lowers it by 1.1 per second. Moving faster raises it by your speed × 0.004 per second: about 0.8 per second at a full 200-unit-per-second run.915
  • The activation flash is a blue light with a 96-unit radius.10 The firing flash lasts 0.1 seconds.11

docs.title: What doesn't break it

docs.title: Vision modes
docs.text:
Every class has a vision mode you can switch on and off. Each class gets a different one.

Vision modes are free. They cost no AUX, have no time limit, and switch off when you die or respawn.1 You can toggle at most once every 0.1 seconds.2

Mode Classes Highlights Reveals cloak? Night vision Recon Nothing specific: brightens the whole scene No Motion vision Assault Any moving model Yes, while the target moves Thermal vision Support Uncloaked players, NPCs, bodies No; also sees through smoke

docs.title: Night vision
docs.text:
Night vision screenshot

Recon uses night vision. It's a screen filter only: it brightens everything, but doesn't draw any player or object differently.3

docs.title: Motion vision
docs.text:
Motion vision screenshot

The Assault uses motion vision. Anything that moves is highlighted, including players, physics props and cloaked players.4 A target that stands completely still isn't highlighted.

Technical details

Along with the screen filter, any model moving faster than 0.5 units per second is drawn again with a highlight material.4

docs.title: Thermal vision
docs.text:
Thermal vision screenshot

The Support uses thermal vision. Uncloaked players, NPCs and bodies show up hot, and you can see through smoke.56

Cloaked players don't show up hot. They look normal, which makes thermal a poor counter to thermoptic camouflage.7

Technical details

The bodies drawn hot are ragdolls and gibs. Thermal vision switches off the smoke screen overlay, which is how Support sees through smoke.56

docs.title: Suppressed weapons
docs.text:
Suppressed variants (marked S) have no muzzle flash. Firing one doesn't make your cloak flash either.

  • the MX-S has penetration 18, against the MX's 38
